title: Experimental Investigation for the Structural Behavior of Composite Beams with Web Openings
content: In this study, the behavior of composite beams with circular web openings was examined to evaluate their performance in integrating mechanical, electrical, and plumbing (M.E.P.) systems while maintaining structural behavior. Six models of composite beams were prepared with different experimental parameters, including the absence, the number, and the locations of the openings within the web under monotonic loading until failure. The first specimen without openings. The second specimen had two openings in the middle of the beam, with a spacing of 500 mm between them. The third specimen had two openings immediately below the load application area. The fourth specimen also contained two openings, but in the shearing zone. The last sample contained ten openings, with a spacing of 250 mm between each opening. The experimental results showed a clear sequence based upon the location of the openings when arranging the effects. The shear zone openings showed the best performance with the least loss in ultimate load of 2.13%, making it the preferred location for service openings. The holes located in the middle of the beam (mid-span) or near the load point caused a medium to large reduction ranging from 9.62% to 11.70% due to the interference/effect of high bending stresses. The results confirm that location is more important than the number or density of openings; this is shown by the fact that the sample with ten openings achieved a reduction in ultimate load similar to that of the two-opening configurations when the openings are concentrated in critical areas. These results support a location-driven design philosophy, whereby strategic placement can significantly reduce structural penalties, independent of the number of openings within the test range used for 80-mm-diameter openings.
